title: A High‐Throughput Hydroponic Assay for Rapidly Screening Drought Tolerance in Potato
author: Zahid, Kieu
materials: Stem internode segments (∼1 cm) from healthy, sterile donor plants
Murashige & Skoog (MS) basal salt mixture including vitamins

steps.title: Generate axenic potato plantlets
steps.instruction: Induce shoots from axillary buds of tissue‑cultured internode cuttings, then excise the new shoots and root them on agar medium to obtain uniform, axenic plantlets with roots at least 1 cm long and vigorous green shoots.

substeps.instruction: Collect internode cuttings from sterile tissue culture and isolate axillary buds.
Culture buds on shoot‑induction medium to generate new shoots.
Excise the newly formed shoots and place them on agar rooting medium.
Incubate until roots reach ≥1 cm and shoots appear healthy.

steps.title: Assemble tip‑box hydroponic units
steps.instruction: Convert standard pipette tip boxes into autoclavable hydroponic vessels, sterilize them, and prepare for plantlet transfer.

substeps.instruction: Disassemble pipette tip boxes and re‑configure them into open containers suitable for holding liquid culture.
Autoclave the assembled tip‑box units to ensure sterility.
Add the appropriate liquid growth medium to each unit.

steps.title: Transfer and pre‑condition plantlets
steps.instruction: Move rooted plantlets from solid agar to the tip‑box hydroponic system and allow a 14‑day acclimation period before imposing drought stress.

substeps.instruction: Gently remove plantlets from agar, rinsing roots with sterile water to eliminate agar residue.
Place each plantlet into a tip‑box unit containing liquid medium.
Maintain the hydroponic setup for 14 days to let roots adapt morphologically and physiologically to solution culture.

steps.title: Prepare and apply PEG drought stress
steps.instruction: Make a polyethylene glycol (PEG) solution at the required concentration, dissolve it completely, cool to room temperature, and expose the pre‑conditioned plantlets to this solution.

substeps.instruction: Weigh PEG and add sterile water to achieve the specified concentration (exact value as per experimental design).
Stir until the solution is fully dissolved.
Allow the solution to cool to room temperature to avoid temperature shock.
Replace the hydroponic medium with the PEG solution for the designated stress period.

steps.title: Rinse roots after PEG stress
steps.instruction: Perform at least four vigorous rinses of the roots with fresh sterile water to remove residual PEG and terminate osmotic stress.

substeps.instruction: Remove the PEG solution from each tip‑box.
Add fresh sterile water and gently agitate to dislodge PEG.
Discard the water and repeat the rinse three more times, ensuring vigorous washing each time.

steps.title: Collect post‑stress phenotypic data
steps.instruction: Document visual symptoms, measure fresh weight, and assess photosynthetic efficiency (quantum yield of PSII) of each plant after the recovery period.

substeps.instruction: Capture high‑resolution images of each plant for visual phenotype scoring.
Harvest shoots and roots, blot dry, and record fresh weight.
Measure PSII quantum yield using a chlorophyll fluorometer according to standard protocols.
